subject: Biology
_transcription: Biology = pages p01-p04 of 2022-eng-IAT.pdf (printed 'Page 2'-'Page 4' on p02-p04; p01 carries no footer). Printed numbers 1-15, checked unbroken: p01 Q1-Q3 (Q3 options B-D run onto p02), p02 Q4-Q8, p03 Q9-Q14 (Q14 stem only), p04 Q14's four option diagrams then Q15. Q1's two columns are printed as a picture of unequal length (4 vs 6 entries) and typed as a pipe table with the extra Column II rows left blank in Column I. Q2's four reactions are typed. Picture options: Q14 (p04), mitochondrial membrane diagrams, read from a 160 dpi zoom.

rows.text:
Match the features of a plant cell listed in Column I with their corresponding examples in Column II.

| Column I | Column II |
|---|---|
| i. Cell with cytoplasm and no nucleus | p. Pollen grain |
| ii. Cell lacking both cytoplasm and nucleus | q. Synergid |
| iii. Cell containing more than two nuclei | r. Tracheid |
| iv. Haploid cell produced by mitosis | s. Tapetum |
| | t. Mature sieve tube |
| | u. Phloem companion cell |

Choose the CORRECT combination from the options below.
options: i and t; ii and r; iii and s; iv and q
i and u; ii and r; iii and s; iv and p
i and u; ii and r; iii and q; iv and p
i and r; ii and t; iii and s; iv and q

rows.text:
Shown below are some of the reactions that occur in the metabolic pathway leading to complete oxidation of glucose during aerobic respiration.

i. Pyruvate \(\longrightarrow\) Acetyl CoA
ii. Dihydroxy acetone phosphate \(\longrightarrow\) Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
iii. Oxaloacetate \(\longrightarrow\) Citrate
iv. Fumarate \(\longrightarrow\) Malate

Choose the CORRECT sequence of reactions during the complete oxidation of glucose.

In a given species of flowering plant, the colour of the seeds is exclusively determined by the colour of its seed coat. Seed coat colour in this species is governed by a nuclear gene with two alleles. The WHITE (\(W\)) allele is dominant over brown (\(w\)) allele. If a plant with brown seeds (\(ww\)) is crossed as a female with pollen from a white seed (\(WW\)) plant, what will be the seed colour and the genotype of the embryo in the resultant seeds obtained from this cross?
During the CoVID-19 pandemic, SARS-CoV2 virus mutated multiple times giving rise to many variants. What is the genetic material of the SARS-CoV2 virus?
Lymph is an important body fluid. Choose the INCORRECT statement about the lymph.
options: It remains as an interstitial fluid and is never put back into circulation.
It is the interstitial fluid generated by the passage of liquid between the cells of the capillary.
It is colourless and has similar mineral composition as of plasma.
Fat digested in the intestine is absorbed through the lymph.

rows.text: Interneurons play an important role in the execution of spinal cord-mediated reflex action. Where are these interneurons located?
Osmoreceptors are sensitive to changes in ionic concentrations and volumes of body fluids. Which among the following best describes the function of these osmoreceptors?
options: They stimulate hypothalamus to facilitate the release of the anti-diuretic hormone and increase water reabsorption.
They stimulate pituitary gland to facilitate the secretion of mineralocorticoids to adjust the changes in mineral composition of the body fluid.
They stimulate atrial wall to release atrial natriuretic factor to induce vasodilation and reduce blood pressure.
They stimulate renin production to induce vasoconstriction and increase blood pressure.

rows.text: A single point mutation in gene 'X' results in breathing difficulty, hypertension as well as partial sterility. Which among the following phenomenon best explains the observed phenotypes?

In a cross between individuals of the genotypes PpQQRrSS and ppqqRrSS, what will be the expected number of progenies with the genotype ppQQRrSS in a population of 400 individuals, assuming independent assortment?
Organisms in which of the following phyla are triploblastic, acoelomate and have bilateral symmetry?

Consider the following biomes: Tropical Rainforest (\(P\)); Tundra (\(Q\)); Desert (\(R\)) and Coastal zone (\(S\)). Choose the most probable descending order of Net Primary Productivity of these biomes.

Nine percent of a population cannot taste a certain food item because of a recessive allele of the gene IAT. Assuming the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what will be the frequency of dominant and recessive alleles, respectively?

rows.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
rows.text: As opposed to DNA replication within the cell, discontinuous synthesis of DNA does NOT occur in a polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Why?
options: Denaturation step in PCR substitutes for the replication fork and Taq polymerase extends DNA only in the 5' to 3' direction.
The replication fork is formed and Taq polymerase extends DNA in both 3' to 5' and 5' to 3' direction.
Denaturation step in PCR substitutes for the replication fork and Taq polymerase extends DNA only in the 3' to 5' direction.
The replication fork is formed and DNA ligase activity of the Taq polymerase joins the discontinuous fragments.

rows.text: Which of the following figures CORRECTLY represents the chemiosmotic hypothesis of ATP synthesis occuring in a mitochondrion in a cell? (Keys for the figure; IMS: Intermembrane space, IMM: Inner mitochondrial membrane, MM: Mitochondrial matrix, ETC: Electron transport chain)
options: ETC moves \(\mathrm{H^+}\) from MM up into IMS; the ATP synthase head sits on the MM side, \(\mathrm{H^+}\) passes through ATP synthase from IMS down into MM, and ADP becomes ATP on the MM side
ETC moves \(\mathrm{H^+}\) from MM up into IMS; the ATP synthase head sits on the IMS side, \(\mathrm{H^+}\) passes through ATP synthase from IMS down into MM, and ADP becomes ATP on the IMS side
ETC moves \(\mathrm{H^+}\) from IMS down into MM; the ATP synthase head sits on the MM side, \(\mathrm{H^+}\) passes through ATP synthase from MM up into IMS, and ADP becomes ATP on the MM side
ETC moves \(\mathrm{H^+}\) from IMS down into MM; the ATP synthase head sits on the IMS side, \(\mathrm{H^+}\) passes through ATP synthase from MM up into IMS, and ADP becomes ATP on the IMS side
